long_biography.plain_text:
Emmerich entered Munich's film school intending to study production design, then changed direction after seeing Star Wars. His unusually ambitious graduation feature, The Noah's Ark Principle, opened the 1984 Berlin Film Festival and led to Centropolis, the company he formed with producer Ute Emmerich. English-language science fiction became his route from German independent production to Hollywood.

Universal Soldier and Stargate established Emmerich in the American studio system, while Independence Day made his large-scale blend of spectacle, ensemble action and landmark destruction internationally recognizable. He continued that approach through Godzilla, The Day After Tomorrow and 2012, alongside more intimate historical films. Decades later, he moved into episodic television by directing half of Those About to Die, a drama set around ancient Rome's entertainment industry.
